data.body: **Backwards-incompatible.** The django stats app writes to its own sqlite database by default (`huey-stats.db` in `settings.BASE_DIR`), instead of `DATABASES['default']`. To keep recording in your main Django database, specify the database explicitly: ```python HUEY_STATS = {'database': 'postgresql://user:password@localhost/my_db'} ``` `HUEY_STATS['database']` takes a db-url or a peewee `Database`, or use `HUEY_STATS['filename']` to set the sqlite path. See the Django docs section for building a peewee database from your existing `DATABASES` entry. The admin *Events* log is now rendered from the stats database through peewee, rather than being a `ModelAdmin` via ORM. It is now linked from the dashboard's *Recent events* heading. --- Consumer: * Add `--shutdown-timeout` option to bound graceful shutdown time. * Add `--graceful-signal` option to allow making SIGTERM the graceful shutdown signal (e.g. ``-g TERM``). User-facing APIs: * Add `ttl` to `lock_task()` and `put_if_empty()` so locks expire on their own. Supported by memory and redis storages, others raise `NotImplementedError`. `RedisHuey` requires server hash-field TTL support (redis 7.4+ or valkey 9+), `RedisExpireHuey` works on any version. * Add `timeout` parameter to `aget_result()`. Small stuff: * Ensure one raising signal receiver does not prevent the remaining receivers from running. * Fix crontab ranges with a step (`0-30/5`) and wrap-around ranges (`22-2`, `day_of_week='1-7'`). Raise `ValueError` when a field matches no values. * Pass failed chord members to the callback as `huey.Error` and skipped (revoked, expired, cancelled) members as `huey.SKIPPED` instead of a raw exception or `None`. * Delete chord partial results explicitly on completion, so they no longer linger until expiry on `RedisExpireStorage`. * Write the error of a failed pipeline stage to every skipped downstream stage, so their `Result` handles raise instead of blocking. * Accept an explicit `id` in `TaskWrapper.s()`, matching `schedule()`. Storage: * Skip messages that fail to deserialize in `Huey.pending()` and `Huey.scheduled()`, logging the error, as `read_schedule()` already does. * Add `clean_name` option to `RedisHuey` (default to `True`). Specify `False` to stop stripping non-alphanumeric characters from the storage namespace. The default will change in a future release. * Reduce Redis round-trips for `peek_data`, `pop_data` and `delete_data`, and make `RedisExpireStorage.incr()` set the TTL atomically w/ the increment. * Skip the exclusive lock in `SqliteStorage.dequeue()` when the queue is empty, so idle consumers no longer block producers and the scheduler. * Batch the `SqliteStorage.read_schedule()` delete to avoid sqlite's parameter limit when many tasks come due at once. Same fix in `SqlHuey`. * Order `SqliteStorage.read_schedule()` and `SqlHuey.read_schedule()` by `(timestamp, id)`, matching `PostgresStorage`. * Add `queue` to the sqlite task index (`task_queue_priority_id`) so queues sharing a file no longer scan each other's rows. The old `task_priority_id` index is dropped when the schema is initialized. I'll get rid of the temporary in-band drop in a few releases. * Add `peek_many()` to the storage API. Revocation checks now fetch the task and task-class keys in one round trip. * Return str keys from `result_items()` on every storage backend. Redis and File storage previously returned bytes. Stats: * Better handling for `timeout`, `locked`, `rate-limited` and `retrying` in stats recorder. * Log dropped events in the stats recorder instead of failing silently. * Fix stats recorder `max_events` pruning to count rows per queue. With multiple queues sharing a stats db, each queue retained only a fraction of the configured cap. * Add `inflight_hours` option to stats recorder, replacing the hardcoded 6 hour in-flight cutoff. * Require the `change_hueydashboard` permission for the django admin dashboard's revoke, restore and flush controls. Previously any staff user who could view the dashboard could also flush the queue. * Add `huey[stats]` extra which installs ol' peewee. [View commits](https://github.com/coleifer/huey/compare/3.3.4...3.4.0)

* Forward the Django database `OPTIONS` when setting up the stats recorder connection. Fixes / replaces #907. * Remove accidental `sqlite3` access at module scope, #908. [View commits](https://github.com/coleifer/huey/compare/3.3.2...3.3.3) Good things come in 3's!

* Flush buffered stats in the worker shutdown hook. Fixes issue where recycled workers might drop some writes. * Store the `FileLock` fd per-thread. Under thread contention the shared fd was clobbered and released by the wrong thread, leaking a held flock and wedging every process using that storage path. `FileHuey` with the default thread workers deadlocked on first contention. [View commits](https://github.com/coleifer/huey/compare/3.3.1...3.3.2)

* Ensure traceback is stored properly for error results. * Restart the stats recorder in forked children via `os.register_at_fork`. Previously the writer thread existed only in the process that called `enable_stats()`, so a consumer w/ `worker_type='process'` (or a preforking web server that loads the app before forking) buffered task events in its workers but never wrote them, and the dashboard showed tasks stuck on "enqueued". [View commits](https://github.com/coleifer/huey/compare/3.3.0...3.3.1)

data.title: Stop sibling result polling when an async group fails
data.body:
When one result in `aget_result_group()` raises, `asyncio.gather()` leaves the other result pollers running. A missing result can then be polled indefinitely after the caller has already received the error.

Keep references to the result-wait tasks and cancel and await any unfinished ones before returning or propagating an exception. This stops only local result polling; queued Huey tasks are not revoked. Tests cover failure cleanup, continued execution of the queued task, caller cancellation, and existing successful group results.

Validation:
- The failure-cleanup regression fails on unchanged `dbd1aef`; the other five asyncio tests pass there.
- Python 3.13.14: 135 asyncio/API/wrapper/immediate-mode tests pass. Python 3.10.20: all six asyncio helper tests pass.
- `git diff --check` passes. The full backend/consumer test suite was not run.

data.title: How to create a dead-letter-queue for tasks that can't be executed?
data.body:
Hey, I've been having fun where sometime we run into a task that's scheduled but which can't be run.

As an example of how this can happen, suppose that you schedule a task to persistent storage but then delete the code that would actually run it and restart the Huey workers.  Now there's a scheduled task that can't run and which will throw an exception when it gets to here.  It'll also stay on the queue, which means the scheduler will keep trying to rerun it. 
https://github.com/coleifer/huey/blob/master/huey/registry.py#L49

(Other ways this could happen include things like a bad custom serializer/deserializer, etc.)

What's the right way to catch errors such as this and make sure that tasks which're in that state don't stay queued?

If it's of any use, I'm happy to send a patch for [api.py:deserialize_task()](https://github.com/coleifer/huey/blob/master/huey/api.py#L299) to add a callback for if a task can't be deserialized?  That way people could decide what to do with it themselves?

>Now there's a scheduled task that can't run and which will throw an exception when it gets to here. It'll also stay on the queue, which means the scheduler will keep trying to rerun it.

What do you mean the scheduler will keep trying to rerun it? If the task was not found, then the scheduler just throws it out. It's easy to demonstrate this and verify for yourself. When the scheduler attempts to run the task that no longer exists/can't be executed, it will throw something like `huey.exceptions.HueyException: tasks.will_be_gone not found in TaskRegistry` and the task is discarded. It no longer remains in the schedule or the queue at that point.

If you want to catch these yourself you can just subclass `RedisHuey` or whatever and implement your own `deserialize_task()` that does what you want with the message.

Thanks for the incredibly fast response!  My apologies, I was wrong there in thinking that the scheduler kept those on the queue.

Just to make sure that I understand: if I subclass RedisHuey I'll be able to catch errors in deserialization but not if the task doesn't exist in the registry?  Oh, I suppose I could add a custom check in the deserialize_task() call to see if the task name is in the registry before create_task() is called?
No that's incorrect - you *will* be able to catch those errors inside `deserialize_task()`.

Sorry, one last quick question - when the scheduler gets the next batch of tasks to work though, what happens if just one of those were to have the sort of problems mentioned above?  Would just that task be thrown out?  Or would the entire batch be removed?

~~It would hardly be robust if the whole batch was removed... Only the problematic task is removed.~~

Hold up, let me make absolutely sure about this, you may have a good point and I missed something!

You were absolutely right -- if a bad task was mixed in a batch of tasks that were ready to transition from the schedule -> main queue, then that whole batch of tasks would be lost! This is now fixed - the tasks are deserialized individually when reading the schedule and an exception is logged if one or more of them fails.
Much appreciated, thank you!

@coleifer, I'm not sure what schedule you usually follow for releasing new versions, but would you mind cutting a patch release that includes this fix?

(On a side note, I'm happy to contribute some of my work engineering time to help with Huey if there's ever anything you'd like a hand with.  We make use of Huey so I feel like we should pay some of that back.)
2.5.2 should be on pypi now.

Store the real traceback in build_error_result

build_error_result called traceback.format_exc() to fill the 'traceback'
field of a failed task's error result, but it runs outside the except
block that handled the exception. In Python 3 format_exc() only reflects
the currently-handled exception, so once control leaves the handler it
returns 'NoneType: None' -- every stored task error had a useless
traceback (the logged traceback was fine, since logging happens inside
the handler).

Format the exception's own __traceback__ instead, which does not depend
on being inside a handler. This matches how the Django contrib backend
(huey/contrib/djhuey/tasks_backend.py) already captures the traceback.

data.body:
When you enqueue a task by calling the wrapped function, e.g. `r = send_email(...)`, then `r` is your result handle. This handle allows you to access the result of running the task after the consumer executes it - similarly, if the task failed with an exception, the result handle will raise an exception if you resolve it. When a task fails and is retried (because you specified 1 or more `retries`) then the result handle can continue to be used to check on the results of the retries. So that is one way -- you can use the result handle to see if the task failed or not.

You can alternatively add a [signal handler](https://huey.readthedocs.io/en/latest/signals.html) so that if a task failed with an unhandled exception, your signal handler will be invoked. This is easiest if you don't want to keep a result handle around and blocking on resolving it / etc.

Ultimately this is the nature of an asynchronous task queue... You will have to decide how to handle them. Your errors don't disappear into a black hole - they are observable via the result handle, stored in the result store itself, and visible to signal handlers. They are also logged, so you can attach a custom log handler as well.

Hello @coleifer thank you for the thourough answer. I mainly want to use the tasks in a request/repsonse cycle from a django web app so I can't really save the response for using/checking it later. 

I took a peek at the signals and saw a `SIGNAL_ERROR` and a `SIGNAL_RETRYING`, however there's no `SIGNAL_ERROR_NO_RETRIES` i.e a way to get signals of tasks that have failed and won't be retried. Am I missing something ? 

I guess I could skip retrying and handle all tasks that error out?
Signal handlers are called with the task instance so you can add an error handler and check the task instances `task.retries` attribute.
Excellent ! Thank you for clarifying
Questions belong on SO, the issue tracker is for issues.

items.title: Store the real traceback in build_error_result
items.body:
### Problem

A failed task's error result carries a `traceback` field, but it is always the string `'NoneType: None\n'` instead of the real traceback:

```python
from huey import MemoryHuey
from huey.exceptions import TaskException

huey = MemoryHuey(results=True)

@huey.task()
def boom():
    raise ValueError('kapow')

r = boom()
huey.execute(huey.dequeue())
try:
    r.get()
except TaskException as e:
    print(repr(e.metadata['traceback']))   # "'NoneType: None\n'"
```

`error` and `task_id` are correct — only the traceback is lost. Every failed task is affected.

### Cause

`Huey.build_error_result` fills the field with `traceback.format_exc()`:

```python
def build_error_result(self, task, exception):
    tb = traceback.format_exc()
    ...
```

but it is called from `_execute` *after* the `try/except` that handled the task's exception has already completed. In Python 3, `traceback.format_exc()` reflects the currently-handled exception only while inside the `except` block; once control leaves the handler `sys.exc_info()` is cleared, so it returns `'NoneType: None'`. (The `logger.exception(...)` call logs the real traceback because it runs inside the handler — the stored result does not.)

### Fix

Format the exception's own `__traceback__`, which doesn't depend on being inside a handler:

```python
tb = ''.join(traceback.format_exception(
    type(exception), exception, exception.__traceback__))
```

This is the same approach the Django contrib backend already uses (`huey/contrib/djhuey/tasks_backend.py`).

### Tests

Extended `test_api.py::test_task_error` to assert the stored `metadata['traceback']` contains the error class and message. It fails on `master` (`'NoneType: None\n'`) and passes with the fix.

# Draft GitHub issue — Huey 3.4.0

## Title
Potential loss of due SQLite scheduled tasks when enqueue fails after schedule removal

## Body
Hi — I found what looks like a reliability gap in Huey 3.4.0's SQLite scheduled-work transfer path.

### Suspected sequence

In the inspected SQLite path, due scheduled rows are removed by the schedule read/dequeue operation, then the scheduler enqueues the returned tasks individually. If an enqueue raises after removal but before every task has been inserted into the task queue, the remaining due tasks may no longer be present in either the schedule table or the queue.

### Controlled source-slice fixture

I ran a local SQLite source-slice fixture against digest-pinned Huey 3.4.0 `storage.py` / `consumer.py` inputs. The fixture uses 503 due tasks (including the apparent 500-record deletion boundary), a future scheduled task, and a task in another queue.

| injected enqueue failure point | queued due tasks after reopen | missing due tasks |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| none (control) | 503 | 0 |
| before first enqueue | 0 | 503 |
| after one enqueue | 1 | 502 |
| after 500 enqueues | 500 | 3 |

The future scheduled task and the other-queue records remained intact in these fixture cases.

### Scope / limitations

This is **not** a claim about security, data durability under power loss, concurrency, or all Huey backends. It is a bounded SQLite/source-slice result with injected enqueue failures. I have not yet run a whole-package production configuration or real process-crash reproduction, so I am reporting this as a potential correctness/recovery issue rather than a confirmed production defect.

### Question

Is loss of unqueued due scheduled tasks after an enqueue exception intentional? If not, would an atomic transfer / recovery-marker approach be appropriate, so a failed transfer leaves scheduled rows retryable rather than deleting them before all queue inserts succeed?

I can provide the small standalone fixture and the exact source hashes if that would help maintainers reproduce or assess this.

This is a longer running task that is often interrupted ``` def scrape_page_set(pages: list[Page], threads: int, blacklist_file: str): blacklist = Blacklist.from_file(blacklist_file) scraper = Scraper(blacklist) return scraper.scrape(pages, threads) def scrape_pages(ctx:Context): .... pages = pages_manager.get_top_unscraped_pages(max_pages_scraped, scrape_minimum_views, d) tasks = [] for i in range(0, len(pages), 20): page_set = pages[i : i + 20] tasks.appendPipeline.scrape_page_set_task(page_set, threads, ctx["scraping_config"].blacklist_file)) for task_result in tasks: try: result: list[Page] = task_result.get( blocking=True, timeout=60 ) # This strategy requires at least 2 workers, as this worker will block while waiting for the results except Exception: task_logger.exception("Failed to get task result") continue ...... ``` As you can see in the log snippet, we see the Main Process receiving the SIGINT, Worker-3 acknowledges that the scrape pages task was interrupted and re-enqueues it . items.title: Add exception call to AsyncResult after task failing
Silence exception log when retrying
items.body:
Hey,

Our use case is similar to this one - https://github.com/coleifer/huey/issues/280 - if an error is logged it triggers an alarm, and we don't really want this to happen if the error has been "handled" by being retried - only if all of the retries have failed and the error is still occurring.

There's a commit linked to that issue that would have allowed me to fix this by just doing 

```python
except Exception:
  task.retries -= 1
  raise RetryTask()
```

But that functionality seems to have since been removed - `task.retries` goes down to 0 but it keeps retrying. 

How would you recommend that we handle this now, given that the task decorator currently includes a number of retries and we'd quite like it to keep obeying that?

items.title: huey.result() won't raise TaskException if task failed with an exception
items.body:
Sample code:

```python
# config.py
from huey import RedisHuey

huey = RedisHuey()
```

```python
# task.py
from config import huey


@huey.task()
def failed():
    raise ValueError("failed!")
```

```python
# main.py
from config import huey
from task import failed
```

then run:
```ipython
In [1]: from config import huey

In [2]: from task import failed

In [3]: r = failed()

In [4]: e = huey.result(r.task.task_id)

In [5]: type(e)
Out[5]: huey.utils.Error
```
It will return an `Error` object instead of raising a exception, but [doc](https://huey.readthedocs.io/en/latest/api.html#Huey.result) said a `TaskException` wiil be raised.

items.title: Retries, results, blocking and exceptions.
items.body:
Hello @coleifer,
       As always, enjoy and appreciate this project and your continued efforts.  Lot of great progress and support; thank you.  I did have a topic I wanted to raise RE task retries, blocking or non blocking, results and exceptions.  

I believe somewhere ~ 2.0 `store_errors` was deprecated.  Prior to `store_errors` being deprecated one could fairly reliably ensure (errors were not "results") that a task with retries would not return a (source code driven) result (`None` or other) until all retries were complete; very easy to accomplish programmatically.  However, now when raising an exception, within a task to trigger a retry, the task result raises an exception where it used to return `None`.  Simplest solution for some implementations; `try/except` every request for the task result and handle appropriately.     

For `blocking=True, timeout=10` however it's a bit different.  Lets assume we are blocking for a task with retries such as `retries=2, retry_delay=3, context=True`.  And lets also say this task is making HTTP/S requests and is using the `retries=2` to account for multiple hosts or perhaps just remote HTTP/S errors; not advocating or endorsing the implementation just using as example.  The caller would rely upon the `blocking=True` to carry out the 2 attempts and return the ultimate result, however if the first task attempt raised an exception the blocking would be satisfied/unblocked by the exception.  If the ultimate result requestor was an HTTP/S based consumer they would be forced into an async OR the server side implementation would have to, off the worker/io process/thread, loop, then try/except to account for the first exception to get to the result of the second try.

I am wondering if a slight devaluing of `blocking=True` took place in the deprecation of `store_errors` within context of tasks with retries.  I am also wondering if there is not an opportunity within `get_raw_result/get`, via task decoration, to enable the suppression of exceptions (as they may be handled in consumer code).  I'd be very interested in hearing your thoughts.  

Thanks and keep the rubber side down. ;-)

items.title: retry without logging an "unhandled exception"
items.body:
There are some situations where I use Huey and I want a task to be tried, but I don't want an error logged in my logging system because the error is being "handled", it's just the handling involves a retry. 

Adding the error to the logging system pollutes my logs and hides real unhandled errors. 

For example, I use Huey to make API calls against a system. Due to some timing issues, the API call may fail now, but will pass in the future, so I retry the task later. The failure, however, is totally normal and expected. But the only way to get Huey to retry later is to let the exception bubble up, which logs the error, even though it is an expected condition. 

As another example, I fail to get a lock on some resource, and I can't run the task. There is no exception here, I just need to retry later. But the only way is to make up a new exception and raise it, again, filling up the logs with errors that are perfectly normal. 

Probably the easiest solution I can propose is to add a new exception that tasks can raise like `RetryException`, which would cause a retry to occur, but would not be logged as an unhandled exception. I can provide a patch for this if the idea is approved.
